topic.title: The ₹350 chair
topic.claim: Half of what you pay for café coffee is rent on a chair, because our cities have almost nowhere free to sit.
topic.moment: You buy a cold coffee you don't want so you can take a call for an hour.

turn.actually: We're paying for a seat, a plug and Wi-Fi, with the coffee as the ticket.

topic.feeling: Like I'm paying an entry fee to exist in my own city.
topic.villain: Cities with almost no free public places to sit: few libraries, parks or plazas
topic.because: When the only places to sit are ones that sell something, the café can price the seat. The menu is just how it bills you.
topic.payoff: Would you buy that coffee if you could sit in a park with Wi-Fi? Then you know what you paid for.
topic.behaviour: People work, date and take calls from cafés, buying one drink per hour as rent.
topic.mechanism: Scarce free space lets private places charge for sitting.
topic.group: Young professionals in metros, often in shared flats
topic.send_to: The friend who 'works from a café' three days a week
topic.why_now: Hybrid work has filled cafés with laptops on weekdays.
real_details: A r/hyderabad post says the poster doesn't want more cafes and wants clean parks and public spaces instead. The thread text includes no comments, numbers or personal stories.

score.why: The café coffee is the ticket for a chair. Cities with nowhere free to sit explain it, and the line reads as an everyday observation, not a complaint.
